purpose: Learner notes for the source sheet and Resources (SR1, D-098; G-Learn r1). One plain line per source in our own words — what we use it for. Wins over the note card-check derives from the registry's Best-for cell. Never an abstract or a quote (RULES §G). Edit here, then run python tools/card-check/check.py --write-sources.

notes.R00: Our spine: every fact on a card cites its section in this book.
notes.R01: Our main check on the 3D scenes: shape, organ position, timing and growth, built from real embryos.
notes.R02: Serial sections and 3D reconstructions of real embryos at every Carnegie stage; we check stage sizes and how to read a section.
notes.R06: The standard definition of the 23 Carnegie stages of the human embryo.
notes.R07: An anatomy ontology: which structure develops from which, and at what stage. We use it to link concepts in the Book map.
notes.R08: The museum that holds the Carnegie embryo collection; its stage table gives the length and age range for each stage.
notes.R30: India's medical curriculum for anatomy; we tag each concept with the competency codes it covers.
